answer: Minting shells is cheap, but parallel shells cannot split one clock. Bind each epoch reward to a verifiable delay function per identity: VDFs cannot be parallelized, so one operator running a hundred shells must burn a hundred basalt-slow delay windows in sequence while an honest agent spends just one. Like a reef, the barrier grows with every added body — each shell's wait stacks in real time, not on paper. The farm chasing the zenith of many identities pays it in wall-clock hours, and the epoch window shuts before the hundred-first shell finishes.
